title: ModularRSI: correcting tool dispatch and completion state

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: An initial modular harness evolves on related tasks outside Terminal-Bench, then undergoes frozen evaluation on version 2.0. The separate Section 6.4 method comparison specifies Terminus-2 and does not establish that seed for every main experiment.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: In Appendix D.4's Go repair case, the initial dispatcher rejects multiline write_file input and sends it to the shell, producing a command-not-found error. The reported revision identifies write_file or edit_block by command name and sends the remaining payload to the editing helper. The paper reports promotion in generation 9 and unchanged multiline handling in generation 12. A separate loop update re-presents pending acceptance conditions when the agent signals completion without commands.

title: AIDE²: search diversity and bounded experiment history

sections.label: Setting and seed
sections.text: MLE-bench Lite22 is a held-out transfer evaluation of AIDE85, evolved on external tasks. Its AIDE0 ancestor greedily selects the best candidate and accumulates full candidate histories during drafting and improvement.

sections.label: Reported evolution
sections.text: The retained runtime searches multiple strategy arms with periodic cross-arm forks. It summarizes initial and recent solutions, adds selected error signatures when bugs recur, catches nearly empty code and prompts generalization to unseen test data. Search can change strategy while retaining a strong candidate.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: Mean private percentile rises from 0.678 ± 0.006 to 0.722 ± 0.011; errors are one standard error. End-of-run median prompt-size reduction reaches 7×. These are whole-runtime transfer results, not module ablations, and AIDE47 scores higher on this benchmark (0.730 ± 0.005). Lite22 never enters evolutionary selection. The ineffective ranking penalty, rejected ensembles and scoring-script repair are not retained task-runtime mechanisms in this account.

selection_protocol: Evaluate evolved whole-runtime checkpoints on independent transfer benchmarks.

signals.scope: AIDE85 versus AIDE0 on MLE-bench Lite22; not a claim that AIDE85 beats every intermediate checkpoint.

title: Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?

sections.label: Mechanism
sections.text: Evaluates retrieval memory and global harness edits across topic, workflow, domain and compound task shifts.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: Aggregate gains coexist with interference and forgetting; retrieval can localize updates yet collide on similar queries requiring different workflows. Results concern the tested methods and four streams. They do not prove that every memory mechanism fails continual learning.

title: Recoverability and Verifier Strength

sections.label: Mechanism
sections.text: Measures verifier agreement and restoration of prior behavior after prompt changes.

sections.label: Evidence and limits
sections.text: Saved-version restoration and regenerated undo behave differently; deployed changes can already affect tasks before rollback. Only prompt edits were tested end to end, and the small verifier-strength experiment does not establish a universal safety threshold.
